source_diagnostics.classification: Mixed literal formula errors, incomplete proof steps and scope guards; not 29 refuted theorems.

records.finding_and_retained_boundary: The first two displays use reciprocal pullback factors; Section 4.3 uses the correct multiplying factors. Internal normalization error.
Proposition 3.5 omits lambda(t) on nonzero fibres, although page 7 includes it. A logarithm of the parameter norm has finite central value only after the scaling.
The atomic model measure omits b_E despite the preceding nonreduced fibre decomposition. Reduced-fibre formulas cannot be extended with b_E suppressed.
Proposition 3.4 omits the positivity hypotheses required by BE21's regularizable psh measure construction. Later globally generated approximants may meet them; an arbitrary model metric need not.
Chart ideal generators are called elements of the base ring A_r. A model ideal such as (t,x) needs a coordinate generator. Generator norms are taken on the appropriate formal model domains.
Nonlinear degree restrictions are needed for the stated indeterminacy-dimension balance; affine linear automorphisms are not covered by that balance. Scope guard.
The homogeneous coordinate tuple is said to have no common zero away from the origin. A map fixing affine zero contradicts this literal assertion. Regularity supplies the needed assertion on S=0.

V=B union U is confused with the escaping set U; the first-entry norm bound uses the wrong radius, and a rescaled iterate retains the wrong index. Lemma 4.8's recurrence also prints exponent n where d_+ is required. A continuity proof certificate is not obtained from these lines.

A nonzero escape-coordinate tuple does not make its first coordinate invertible on the whole compact set. A product of two Hénon maps with one block fixed at zero witnesses this. The extra constant 1 in log max supplies an additional normalized function; dropping it requires a late-escape bound. Local charts and rank remain inputs to verify.

Nullstellensatz certificate coefficients are asserted to be linear sums of map coefficients. Solving the coefficient system generally needs rational functions/nonzero minors. A uniform-degree meromorphic certificate requires its own argument.

Map-coefficient maxima alone do not give the asserted covering constants; the explicit family below disproves that covering. Certificate coefficients and complex monomial counts are missing, and diagonal membership does not replace forward invariance of the product domain for telescoping.
The affine hybrid projection is incorrectly called proper. The later closed-polydisc argument is the appropriate compactness interface.

Raw degree-D model functions are identified with degree-normalized affine escape approximants, omitting degree division and the reference potential. The good-reduction calculation below disproves the literal identification.
The final projective test integral drops its affine cutoff. Use the extension by zero of chi times the affine test, with chi=1 on the common closed support.

The historical open maximum/product question and the new claimed answer require separate edition-aware status. Neither the old remark nor the new assertion is a certified current open/solved verdict here.

Theorem 1.2/equation (16) has the wrong sign in the total-Lyapunov scaling. The a(t)=t calculation below is a counterexample to this printed formula, not the main weak-convergence theorem. Published 2025 status unverified.

Oseledets concerns derivative products along the orbit, not one-step derivative eigenvalues. The first-exponent proof replaces the cocycle expression without justification. The displayed derivative has +a in place of -a, and the hybrid logarithmic factor is negative. Do not import this proof or first-exponent asymptotic.

On the backward escape region G_- includes minus the logarithm of the coefficient norm divided by d-1. Inverse iterates have leading coefficient a^(-(d^n-1)/(d-1)); they are not monic for general a. Their nonzero weighted leading term can still give the projective morphism.

The raw logarithm at a fixed zero is -infinity; log+ is needed. An absolute error bound has a potentially negative logarithm of the inverse coefficient norm on its right side, and the backward lower estimate reverses its coefficient sign. These lines are not a uniformity certificate.
T_+ and T_- are defined with -ddc of psh escape potentials. The positive curvature convention requires +ddc. The new 2026 preprint uses the positive convention.

The stated normalization of a general map (P(x)-a y,bx) uses c^d rather than c^(d-1)=leading(P), and the printed second coordinate of the conjugation produces b^2 x. The monic b=1 main setting must be separated from this general conjugation claim.
Infimum of generator logarithms does not define the ideal norm: generators (1,t) of the unit ideal give a different value from generator 1 alone. The appropriate formal-domain norm uses a maximum.

The claimed normalized model-function/escape equality omits the Fubini–Study reference potential. The following metric-section calculation partly recovers the required cancellation. Retain the corrected metric interface.

Affine properness and open-polydisc compactness are false as stated. Restricting a projective weak limit to the affine part also needs tightness/common support. No first-countability assumption is introduced.

The selected formulas include unpowered ideals in a degree-matching sum, inf instead of max, missing b_E, and degree/metric mismatch. Correct lambda scaling and fixed-approximant CLN are read in the same edition. Earlier Chapter 66 corrections are preserved.

FS closure, nef/psh regularization and positive/signed products have distinct hypotheses. Example 8.11 first passes to reduced special fibre. The monotonic-shift sentence needs a fast subsequence, already supplied in the book. These are interface guards, not a refutation of BE21.

Lemma 6.2 uses <= instead of strict degree drop and reverses composition order; identity maps disprove the literal equivalence. Individual good-reduction forward/backward equalities need a maximum, and raw-log, exponential/additive and product-height steps have the indicated normalization errors. Do not claim a full published proof audit.

The selected BT interfaces keep their precise class. Page 213's displayed softmax needs exp(x_i/epsilon), and the printed positive-rank inequality is reversed. These auxiliary displays are not used as a rank certificate. No verdict is given on the unneeded Corollary 8.6.7 multiplication wording.

The complex escape-rank/maximum identity and weighted model measure are read directly. Their ambient hypotheses, source layouts and tensor normalizations remain load-bearing; they do not settle the new non-Archimedean dynamical rank statement.
